# FX target redemption forward (`fx-tarf` v1)

Series of leveraged forwards ending when a profit target is hit.

**Asset class:** FX · **Family:** exotic · **Product type:** `FX_TARF`

Applies to trades whose `productType` is `FX_TARF`. Open one with `TRD <tradeId>`.

```sutra
sutra: fx-tarf
version: 1
description: Series of leveraged forwards ending when a profit target is hit.
match: { kind: trade, where: "$.productType == 'FX_TARF'", priority: 10 }
title: { pill: FX · FX target redemption forward, id: $.tradeId, with: "link($.counterparty.id, 'counterparty', $.counterparty.name)" }
strip:
  - { label: Notional, bind: "$.currency + ' ' + fmt($.notional, 'amount0')" }
  - { label: Direction, bind: $.direction }
  - { label: Trade date, bind: $.tradeDate, fmt: date }
  - { label: Maturity, bind: $.maturityDate, fmt: date }
  - { label: MTM (USD), bind: $.mtm, fmt: signed0, tone: sign, emphasis: true }
  - { label: FX delta (USD), bind: $.risk.fxDelta, fmt: signed0, tone: sign }
  - { label: Vega (USD), bind: $.risk.vega, fmt: signed0, tone: sign }
  - { label: Status, bind: $.status, tone: status }
panels:
  - id: terms
    kind: kv
    title: Terms
    code: TRM
    key: F2
    columns:
      - { label: Strike, bind: $.terms.strike, fmt: rate5 }
      - { label: Target (pips), bind: $.terms.target, fmt: amount0 }
      - { label: Leverage, bind: $.terms.leverage }
      - { label: Effective, bind: $.effectiveDate, fmt: date }
      - { label: Counterparty, bind: $.counterparty.name }
  - id: schedule
    kind: ladder
    title: Observations
    code: OBS
    key: F3
    rows: $.schedule
    highlight: "#index == $.nextIndex"
    columns:
      - { label: Date, bind: "@.date", fmt: date }
      - { label: Level, bind: "@.level", fmt: price2 }
      - { label: Trigger, bind: "@.trigger", fmt: price2 }
      - { label: Performance, bind: "@.performance", fmt: pct2, tone: sign }
      - { label: Outcome, bind: "@.outcome", tone: status }
  - { id: built, kind: provenance, title: How this view was built }
  - id: marketData
    kind: line
    title: "FX spot rate: Last 30 days"
    code: FX
    key: F4
    area: right
    source: "link($.fxSpot, 'fx-spot')"
    rows: history
    x: date
    y: mid
    fmt: rate5
  - id: sensitivities
    kind: hbar
    title: FX delta by bucket (USD)
    code: SENS
    area: right
    rows: $.sensitivities
    label: bucket
    value: fxDelta
    fmt: signed0
    tone: sign
  - id: pnl
    kind: line
    title: Daily P&L, last 20 days (USD)
    code: PNL
    area: right
    rows: $.pnlHistory
    x: date
    y: pnl
    fmt: signed0
  - { id: refs, kind: links, title: Linked entities, code: REFS, area: right }
keys: { F7: "link($.nettingSet, 'netting-set')", F8: impact, F9: raw }
```

## Terms

Product-specific terms live under `terms` in the trade document.

| Field | Label | Format |
|---|---|---|
| `terms.strike` | Strike | `rate5` |
| `terms.target` | Target (pips) | `amount0` |
| `terms.leverage` | Leverage | text |

## Market data

Reference fields on the trade point at the market data it is valued with. They show under *Linked entities* and drive F8 impact ("which trades use this curve?").

| Field | Kind | Selected by |
|---|---|---|
| `fxSpot` | `fx-spot` (FX spot rate) | `{pair}` |
| `fxVolSurface` | `fx-vol-surface` (FX volatility surface) | `{pair}` |

## Risk

| Measure | Field | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| FX delta | `risk.fxDelta` | value change for a 1% move in the FX rate |
| Vega | `risk.vega` | value change for a 1 point rise in implied volatility |

The *FX delta by bucket* chart reads `sensitivities[].fxDelta`.

## Observations

`schedule` rows (ladder), F3: `date`, `level`, `trigger`, `performance`, `outcome`. The next event is highlighted (`nextIndex`).

## Layout notes

- The strip leads with size and dates, then MTM (emphasised) and the product's main risk measures.
- F2 is the terms, F3 the schedule, F4 the market data it is most sensitive to; F7 opens the netting set, F8 shows impact and F9 the raw document.
- Common fields (counterparty, netting set, book, trader, MTM, P&L) are described in the pack guide.
